why: It is a ticket business with a physical identity: every piece of clothing is tagged, weighed, priced by rule and tracked until the customer comes back for it.
operator: The owner receives a bag of clothes, and every piece has to be identified, counted, checked for stains, weighed, priced by rule and returned to the same customer. The pain is the lost piece: the customer comes back and one shirt is not in the bag. The second pain is the pricing, because the shop quotes by weight and by rule and the rules are in the owner head.
entities: Shop (id, name, branchId, address, phone, currency, openingHours, taxRegistration)
Ticket (id, branchId, number, customerId, receivedAt, promisedAt, dueAt, status, bagCount, weightGrams, totalPiasters, paidPiasters, note)
TicketItem (id, ticketId, tagNumber, descriptionAr, categoryId, condition, stains, weightGrams, pricePiasters, serviceId, status)
Service (id, nameAr, nameEn, kind, pricePerKgPiasters, pricePerPiecePiasters, turnaroundDays, isExpress)
Sale (id, branchId, customerId, ticketId, lines, totalsPiasters, payments, createdAt, idempotencyKey)
PurchaseOrder (id, supplierId, status, lines, expectedAt, totalPiasters)
StockItem (id, nameAr, unit, costPiasters, quantity, supplierId, reorderPoint)
Shift (id, branchId, openedBy, openedAt, closedAt, floatPiasters, countedPiasters)
LostItem (id, ticketId, tagNumber, reason, reportedAt, resolvedAt)
units: piece, kilogram, gram, and the bag as the intake unit for a customer
batches: Not for the clothes. The stock of the shop (the detergent, the bags, the hangers) is a normal stock list with a reorder point
expiry: Not a driver here. What matters instead is the due date of each ticket: the promised day, and the reminder when the customer does not come back
special: The structures specific to this sector are the tag with a barcode per item, the ticket with the promised time, the express tier, the lost item record, and the customer who has three tickets open
screens: Intake: the customer arrives, the bag is counted, every piece is tagged with a barcode and the photos of the stains are taken, and the ticket prints with the promised day
The tag printer view: the list of the tags with their numbers, ready to print on the thermal printer
The workshop board: the tickets by state (received, washing, ready, delivered) and the ones that are late
Pricing: the weight per piece, the service per category, the express tier, and the total that the counter reads to the customer
Ready for pickup: the tickets that are ready, the customer phone and one tap to call or to send the message
Delivery on the bag: a service where a rider collects the bag and brings it back, with the driver and the time
The customer: their tickets, their history and the unclaimed pieces that are still waiting
End of day: the money, the tickets received, the tickets ready and the pieces not collected
roles: Owner: everything, including the prices, the rules and the reports
Manager: everything except billing, approves the price exceptions and the refunds
Counter: the intake, the tags, the payment and the handover
Washer and ironer: the workshop board and the state of the tickets
Rider: only the collections and the deliveries assigned to him
reports: Tickets received, ready and delivered per day
Revenue per service and per kilogram weight
Late tickets: what was promised and what was delivered late
Unclaimed pieces after fourteen days with their value
Wash and delivery cost per ticket
integrations: Thermal printer through ESC/POS for the ticket and the barcoded item tags
Barcode scanner at the counter to read the tag back when the bag returns
Phone camera for the stain photos, stored with the ticket
WhatsApp for the ready message and the pickup reminder through the shop own account
A weighing scale for the bulk weight
onboarding: Business basics: name, branch, address, phone, currency, opening hours
Services: the categories of clothes and the price per piece and per kilogram, with the turnaround days
Express: the express tiers with the price and the hours
Rules: the stain rules, the excluded items and the turnaround the shop promises
Team: the counter, the workshop and the rider
Suppliers: the detergent, the bags and the hangers
First week plan: receive a bag with three tags, price it, print the tags, mark one ticket ready, send the ready message
seed: Category list in Arabic for the clothes: قميص, بنطلون, جاكيت, فستان, بدلة, ملابس بيضاء, فرش, سجاد
Service templates with the price per piece and the turnaround days
A ticket layout with the bag count, the weight, the promised date and the total
A tag layout with the barcode and the ticket number

landing_en.headline: A laundry where every piece is tagged and followed to the handover
landing_en.sub: Intake with barcoded tags, a price by the kilogram or by the piece, and a clear promised day for the customer
benefits: Every piece carries a barcoded tag, so a missing piece is found immediately
The promised time is recorded with the express tier, and the customer gets a message when it is ready
The pieces nobody collected show up with their value after fourteen days
faq: What if a customer loses a piece? Every piece is tied to the ticket and to the tag, so it is found and returned
Does it work with no connection? Yes: the intake and the printing keep working

pricing: The free tier fits one counter: one business, one branch, two seats, the intake, the tags and the till
Starter adds the workshop board, the ready messages and a year of history
The Business tier adds the express tiers, the pickup reminder, the lost item record and the multi branch collection
The tag printing is priced per device, not per piece

tasks.title: Register the laundry pack in the sector registry
tasks.brief: Add the manifest for laundry in packages/core/src/sectors/registry.ts with the base template service and the modules (pos, tickets, tags, workshop, express tiers, deliveries, shifts), the feature flags, the role templates and the terminology map.
tasks.done: getSector('laundry') returns the manifest and the registry test asserts the modules and the flags.

tasks.title: Write the laundry data model with the tickets and the tags
tasks.brief: Type the entities in packages/core/src/sectors/laundry/schema.ts: tickets with the promised and the due date, the items with the tag number, the condition and the stains, the tags with the barcode, the services with the price per kilogram or per piece, the express tiers and the lost item record.
tasks.done: The schema compiles with no any, the tag number is unique inside a ticket, and the tests pass.

tasks.title: Build the laundry seed with the Arabic categories and the services
tasks.brief: Write packages/core/src/sectors/laundry/seed.ts with the Arabic clothing categories, the service templates, the express tier presets, the ticket layout and the tag layout, and the role templates. No price and no customer is invented.
tasks.done: The seed loads, the test asserts the categories and the services, and it asserts that no price was seeded.

tasks.title: Write the laundry terminology map in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Create packages/ui/src/sector/laundry/glossary.ts with the trade words: تاج, تذكرة, كيس, بقعة, سريع, كجم, and the counter words, in Arabic and English.
tasks.done: The glossary covers every screen of the sector with no generic shop wording and the label test passes.

tasks.title: Build the intake screen with the tags and the photos
tasks.brief: Build the intake: the customer, the bag count, each piece described and tagged with a barcode, the stain photos taken with the phone camera, the weight and the price by the rule, and the ticket that prints with the promised day.
tasks.done: Each piece gets a unique tag, the total matches the weights and the services, the photos attach to the item, and the ticket prints with the promised date.

tasks.title: Build the workshop board with the states
tasks.brief: Build the board where the workshop moves the tickets between the states (received, washing, ready, delivered), with the late tickets highlighted and the promised date visible.
tasks.done: A ticket moves between the states with the user and the time, a ticket past its promised date is flagged, and the counter sees the same board.

tasks.title: Build the pickup reminder and the unclaimed list
tasks.brief: Build the ready for pickup screen: the tickets that are ready, the customer phone, one tap to call or to send the WhatsApp message, and the unclaimed list after fourteen days with the value of the pieces.
tasks.done: The message goes out through the shop own account, the sent state is stored, and the unclaimed list shows the value and the days waiting.

tasks.title: Build the collection and delivery on the bag
tasks.brief: Build the pickup service: the bag collected from the customer, the rider and the time, the ticket created without a counter visit, and the handover back with the same tags.
tasks.done: A collected bag creates a ticket with the tag numbers, the rider sees only his own pickups, and the returned bag matches the tags of the intake.

tasks.title: Build the laundry report pack
tasks.brief: Add the reports of this sector: tickets received, ready and delivered per day, the revenue per service and per kilogram, the late tickets, the unclaimed pieces with their value, the lost items and the cash reconciliation, each with the CSV export.
tasks.done: Every report computes its own numbers, the test matches a manual calculation and the export opens in a spreadsheet.

tasks.title: Publish the laundry landing page in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Build the sector page from the outline: the Arabic headline first, the tagged intake and the workshop board as the proof blocks with real screenshots, the two questions answered, and the English mirror.
tasks.done: The page passes the layout rules at 320 to 1920 px in both languages and both themes, and every claim matches a screen that exists.

risks: The stain photos and the condition of the clothes are personal data of the customer and belong to the shop, so they never enter our analytics and can be deleted on request
The price rules are the shop own, so the app never invents a price for a piece the counter did not describe
A lost piece is recorded as an incident with a reason, and the product never decides who pays
The chemical and the waste rules of dry cleaning belong to the local authority, and the app records the work without advising on it
